messages:
lucy: I opened a compact PR to harmonize the provisioning playbook fields and include a tiny backwards-compat shim for older tenant configs. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference-docs/pull/4728. Main asks: 1) review naming, 2) confirm short SDK snippet + 1-line shim, 3) wording for SLA note.

sam: looking now. we should standardize on `target_utilization_pct` and `cooldown_seconds` across all examples (YAML/TF/SDK/CLI). avoids confusion when folks copy-paste.

marta: agree on field names. for the shim, propose a 1-line mapping in examples: `tenant_label -> isolation_tags = [tenant_label]` and a tiny migration helper in python. keep it brief.

kevin: draft python shim (one-liner in docs): `policy.setdefault("isolation_tags", []).append(policy.pop("tenant_label")) if policy.get("tenant_label") else None` — keeps it compact but maybe cryptic. maybe break into two lines?

ryan: prefer two-line clarity to one-liner. small code block is fine. also add a short note: run migration in staging and verify `redwoodctl capacity describe --tenant <T>` after running.

lucy: ok i'll expand to two lines for readability. also adding a terraform snippet showing reserved + burst pools and a short comment about eviction ordering.

marta: wording suggestion for SLA: "Reserved pools provide latency SLA; burst pools are preemptible and do not provide a latency SLA." short and explicit.

sam: add a CLI example for tenant admins: `redwoodctl capacity set-policy --tenant team-sparrow --policy burst --target 65 --cooldown 300`. keep it in the CLI section.

kevin: SDK snippet (python) I'll add: `client.provision_capacity(tenant_id="team-sparrow", pool_type="burst", policy={"target_utilization_pct":65, "cooldown_seconds":300, "isolation_tags":["team-sparrow"]})` — single-line keeps examples concise.

docs-bot: style checklist: present tense, examples <= 12 lines, include param links, prefer clear naming. :memo:

lucy: thanks. I'll push edits: rename fields, add two-line migration helper, terraform + CLI + SDK one-liners, and the SLA sentence. ping me for any last phrasing tweaks before I merge.
